- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 5 forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently high over 3+ days, model overreacts; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment in final 5 days by +0.5–1.0% per day.
